summary: Siskiyou NF lookout in Coos County: a 40-foot L-4 tower built in 1939 with CCC labor, abandoned in the 1950s and gone.

facts.design: 40-foot wooden tower with an L-4 cab
facts.status_note: Abandoned in the 1950s and gone per the register and Rex's page; Forest Lookouts status line reads Removed with no date; no removal year found

staffing.status: staffed 94 days in 1941; no later staffing found in these sources

events.note: Forest Service announced a new 40-foot tower and station in August 1939; CCC crews under the local ranger built it; described as nearly finished in October 1939
Lookout staffed 94 days; reports went to the Powers Ranger Station
Register and Rex's page say abandoned in the 1950s; 1950 is a placeholder for the decade, not a recorded date
Registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register on October 15, 2019

evidence.supports: 40-foot tower with an L-4 cab built on the site in 1939; abandoned in the 1950s and gone
evidence.quote: A 40 foot tower with a L-4 cab was constructed on the site in 1939. The lookout was abandoned in the 1950's and is gone.

evidence.supports: Forest Service plan for a new 40-foot tower and station, August 1939
evidence.quote: The United States Forest Service reports that a new 40 foot tower and lookout station is to be constructed at Hanging Rock.

evidence.supports: Coos Bay Times, August 19, 1939: CCC building the station under the local ranger
evidence.quote: CCC labor under the supervision of the local ranger, Boyd Rasmussen, is building a new lookout station at Hanging Rock.

evidence.supports: Myrtle Point Herald, August 17, 1939: new 40-foot tower and station planned, with CCC boys under the ranger's supervision doing the building
evidence.quote: CCC boys under the supervision of the ranger will build the project.

evidence.supports: lookout housed in a tent in August 1939
evidence.quote: At present the lookout is housed in a tent.
The new lookout at Hanging Rock is nearly finished and will be complete in about a week.

evidence.supports: newspaper description of the site's coverage of the Rogue River area and South Fork Coquille headwaters
evidence.quote: Hanging Rock provides excellent coverage of the Rogue river area in the Mule creek district as well as over the headwaters of the south fork of the Coquille.

evidence.supports: reports went to Powers Ranger Station over West Coast Telephone line
evidence.quote: The reporting station was the Powers Ranger Station and communications were by way of West Coast Telephone line.

evidence.supports: 1940 guard placement plan: good views of Agness and Galice districts where man-caused fires are likely
evidence.quote: Position has good seen area in the Agness and Galice districts where man-caused fires are apt to occur.

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts status line reads Removed, with no date given
40-foot wooden L-4 tower, abandoned in the 1950s, gone
Hanging Rock listed as an L-4 40-foot wooden tower built 1939 on the Siskiyou NF
Oregon index lists Hanging Rock as a gone tower
registered on the Former Fire Lookout Sites register October 15, 2019

sources.title: Hanging Rock Lookout Site
sources.publisher: Former Fire Lookout Sites Register, Forest Fire Lookout Association

sources.title: Historic Fire Lookouts on the Siskiyou National Forest: Cultural Property Inventory and Request for a Determination of Eligibility to the National Register of Historic Places
sources.publisher: USDA Forest Service, Siskiyou National Forest (hosted by Southern Oregon University Digital Collections)

notes_for_editor: 1939 build and gone status agree across sources. No removal year appears anywhere; the 1950 abandoned event is a placeholder for the 1950s and is labelled as such. Only one staffing record (1941) was found. No source describes the site today or its access, so the story says so. A Hanging Rock rock outcrop with trails on the Powers Ranger District (Panther Ridge area) turned up in search results; nothing read ties it to the lookout site, so the story does not use it. No photos with usable image URLs were found.
